result.summary: Extracts legacy wallet migration methods and the public MigrateLegacyToDescriptor routines out of wallet/wallet.cpp into dedicated wallet/migration.{h,cpp} files. Relocates wallet path and persistent startup setting helper functions to wallet/walletutil.{h,cpp}. Renames wallet/migrate.{h,cpp} to wallet/legacybdb.{h,cpp} to clarify that it handles legacy Berkeley DB storage rather than general migration logic.
result.problem: wallet/wallet.cpp exceeds 4,500 lines and commingles legacy BDB migration logic with core descriptor wallet operations, making the primary wallet implementation difficult to read, maintain, and reason about.
evidence: PR description: 'It has been noted by many developers that the wallet/wallet.cpp file is quite hard to reason about. It is more than 4500 lines long currently and this patch is an attempt to shortern it by around 800 lines by extracting out the wallet migration code into a dedicated wallet/migration.cpp file.'

PR description: 'moves the legacy wallet stuff from the main wallet file that paves the way for it being descriptor specific (as much as possible), and makes legacy wallet migration code a first-class citizen in its own file.'
result.scope_notes: Largely a move-only refactoring across wallet files, including moving utility functions and renaming wallet/migrate to wallet/legacybdb.
result.changed_since_previous: Rebased on master to incorporate recently added migration options and settings, including moving UpdateWalletSetting to walletutil and updating MigrateLegacyToDescriptor signatures.
result.card: Extracts approximately 800 lines of legacy Berkeley DB wallet migration code out of wallet.cpp into a dedicated wallet/migration module. Relocates wallet path and startup setting helpers into walletutil, and renames wallet/migrate to wallet/legacybdb to clarify its purpose. The change is a move-only refactor aimed at reducing the size and complexity of wallet.cpp without modifying runtime behavior.

risk.why: Moving wallet migration and setting persistence functions could introduce regressions in legacy wallet upgrading or startup wallet loading if symbol visibility or logic were inadvertently changed.
